## Goal
`docs/i18n/GLOSSARY_ES.md:3` promises the usted register and one term per concept, but no test reads the glossary.

## Order
Start only after WO-225 is merged (it edits `docs/i18n/GLOSSARY_ES.md`, which this test reads). If a slot frees first, take the next WO and come back.

## Acceptance criteria (testable)
1. Parse the glossary table; every row has three non-empty cells; no English concept appears twice (case-insensitive) with different Spanish.
2. The Spanish column uses no tú forms (a word list in the test: tú, tu, te, contigo, puedes, quieres, tienes, eres, and similar); the usage-note column may mention them.
3. The Spanish column contains none of the Spanish equivalents of the banned positioning words (garantía, garantizar, garantizado, "100 %", "para siempre") per docs/POSITIONING.md.
4. Every bold or quoted English term in `docs/i18n/TRANSLATION_GUIDE.md` that names a glossary concept exists in the glossary, or the test lists it as an exception with a reason.

Fake data only (Jane Q Testperson, Springfield IL). Offline: no network, no sockets (FastAPI `TestClient` is fine), no git, no installs, no new dependencies. Tests must pass on Windows CI too: `tmp_path` and `pathlib`, no hard-coded `/tmp`, no `/`-joined path strings or other POSIX-only assumptions (WO-217 broke windows-latest that way). The module under test is outside Codex's code lane: a real product bug = `pytest.mark.xfail(strict=True, reason=...)` plus a finding with file:line in VENDOR_STATUS.md; never edit it. Check `tests/`, `tests/copilot/`, `tests/codex/` and `tests/grok/` first and don't duplicate a guard. Line numbers are from main at the time of writing; re-check them in your worktree.
